#### 1. autosomal dominant hypocalcemia 2  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.666)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-112043, Reactome:R-HSA-399997, Reactome:R-HSA-428930, Reactome:R-HSA-9860927, Reactome:R-HSA-202040)

Gain-of-function mutations in GNA11 lead to aberrant G protein-coupled receptor signaling, which paradoxically can manifest as either hypercalcemia (familial hypocalciuric hypercalcemia 2) or hypocalcemia (autosomal dominant hypocalcemia 2) depending on the specific downstream effects on calcium-sensing receptor regulation and parathyroid hormone secretion.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of distinct causal genes for each disease, or demonstration that the shared mutations in GNA11 result in loss-of-function rather than gain-of-function for both conditions. _(variant: rs11550290)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the divergent phenotypic outcomes of gain-of-function mutations in the same gene (GNA11) provides critical insights into the complex regulation of calcium homeostasis and can inform therapeutic strategies targeting G protein-coupled receptor signaling pathways.
